obligation: Internal report of a suspected incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6a (binding through the CJIS Security Addendum sec. 3.01; 28 CFR 20.33(a)(7)); POL-03 4.2
trigger: Any staff member suspects an incident (ransom note, unexpected MFA prompt, locked files, lost laptop, FTI found in a company file)
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Operations Manager (incident lead); then Lead Platform Engineer; then owner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - AC-01 contract; POL-03 applies the same 1-hour rule to every incident

obligation: Company notice to the sheriff's office (AC-01) of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; AC-01 contract; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve the AC-01 workspace, SYS-02, the sheriff's file drop, or support tickets from sheriff users
deadline: IR-6b sets no separate deadline. AC-01 contract and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery, without waiting for the company's investigation
notify: AC-01 local agency security officer (LASO), who routes the report to the CJIS Systems Officer (CSO), SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Sheriff's report of a security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty the company supports)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: Addendum sets no deadline; follows the state CSA's procedure
notify: AC-01 reports to the CSO and the Director, FBI, with the actions taken by AC-01 and the company. The FBI may suspend access and require CHRI to be deleted or returned
applies_at_this_tier: AC-01 duty. The company supplies its actions and evidence to AC-01 on request

obligation: Company notice to the prime and the revenue agency of a possible FTI disclosure
citation: N92-R01: Pub. 1075 Exhibit 7 I(3), I(10)-(11) (flowed down in the SC-01 subcontract); sec. 1.8.2; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI: a compromised laptop that connects or connected to the agency virtual desktop, stolen agency credentials, or FTI found in a company system
deadline: Immediately. Company target: within 1 hour of discovery, so the agency keeps most of its 24-hour window
notify: Prime's security officer and the revenue agency's disclosure officer (both, by phone, then in writing with no FTI)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SC-01 subcontract

obligation: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards report of an FTI incident or data breach
trigger: Discovery of a possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, or a data breach. Do not wait for an internal investigation to confirm FTI was involved
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery. The Office of Safeguards data incident report goes at the same time as the TIGTA contact; details follow as known
notify: TIGTA Field Division Special Agent-in-Charge (for network intrusions, TIGTA Electronic Crimes and Intelligence Division) and the IRS Office of Safeguards (encrypted email titled "data incident report", no FTI in it)
applies_at_this_tier: Revenue agency files. Sec. 1.8.2 also places the duty on the individual who discovers a possible improper disclosure, so the company confirms with the prime and the agency within the 24 hours that the report was made, and contacts TIGTA directly if it cannot confirm

obligation: Taxpayer notice and media release review after unauthorized FTI access (agency duty)
trigger: Disciplinary or adverse action is proposed against the agency employee responsible for an unauthorized inspection or disclosure
deadline: Written notice to the taxpayer; the agency confirms completion to the Office of Safeguards and shares any draft media release before distribution
notify: Affected taxpayers; IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No for this runbook: an external attacker is not an agency employee. The media-release step still applies to the agency

obligation: Company notice to the county and city customers (AC-02, AC-03, AC-04)
trigger: Suspected incident affecting a customer's workspace or exports
deadline: Within 1 hour of discovery for suspected ransomware; within 4 hours for other suspected incidents
notify: Each customer's security contact (AC-02 IT security liaison; AC-03 and AC-04 IT managers)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contracts and POL-03

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report (AC-02, AC-03, AC-04)
trigger: Ransomware incident affecting a county or municipality ("local government" in 282.3185(2)), including one in a contractor-hosted system the local government uses
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty. The company supplies the required content in time: summary of facts, date and location of the most recent backup, whether it was affected and cloud-based, types of data, estimated fiscal impact, ransom details. AC-01 is a sheriff's office; it decides with its county whether 282.3185 reaches it, and gets the company's notice within 1 hour either way

obligation: Florida state agency ransomware report (revenue agency)
trigger: Ransomware incident at a state agency, if the incident reaches the revenue agency's systems
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and the FDLE Cybercrime Office
applies_at_this_tier: Revenue agency duty, only if its systems are affected. The company's notice to the prime and the agency (above) gives it the facts

obligation: Local government after-action report
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty for AC-02, AC-03, AC-04. The company provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons learned in time

obligation: Prohibition on ransom payment by Florida agencies
trigger: Ransom demand to a state agency, county, or municipality
deadline: Applies at all times: these customers may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-03 4.7)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds AC-02, AC-03, AC-04, and the revenue agency. The company will not pay over agency data that any customer objects to

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to each affected agency
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) in a system the company maintains for an agency
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected agency. Include all information the agency needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the company as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h))

obligation: Agency notice to Florida individuals
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (for example Social Security numbers in AC-02 records, driver license numbers in city files)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; law enforcement may delay in writing (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company may send notices for an agency only if asked (501.171(6)(b))

obligation: Agency notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; likely for AC-02 (about 7,500 households) if its workspace data was taken. The company supplies counts of Florida residents per workspace

obligation: Agency notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected individuals who live outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty in each state where affected individuals reside; the company supplies residence data

obligation: MSP notice to the company
citation: MSP service contract (24-hour term to be added, POAM-014); POL-03 4.8
trigger: Security incident in the MSP's remote management platform or affecting company laptops or the suite
deadline: Today: no contract term. Target term: within 24 hours
notify: Operations Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual gap. Until the amendment, the company asks the MSP at every incident whether its own tools are involved

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: SP 800-53 IR-6(3) (Moderate baseline); CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving the platform tenant, the IaaS account, or the AI add-on
deadline: No deadline set; as soon as practicable
notify: Platform vendor and IaaS provider security incident channels
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract (SP 800-53 Moderate)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment. Full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
citation: OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) mitigating factor; company practice
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed
deadline: Company target: within 48 hours of declaration
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Coordinate with the agencies, which report to FDLE under Florida law

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: HIPAA breach notification
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Not applicable
notify: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - no customer has designated the company a business associate

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services report
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (SC-01 is a state contract)

obligation: Kaspersky covered article report
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Kaspersky covered article identified under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
